packageRules.description: Dev dependencies: one grouped PR, merged automatically when CI is green. They don't ship, so the PR needs no changeset (the label skips the check)
The private tools' dependencies (prettier in generate-wrappers) are dev tooling too: same PR

Runtime dependencies of the published packages: a range users install, so it changes only when a new release is outside it (bump would narrow it to the newest release). In-range releases reach the lockfile through lock file maintenance
GitHub Actions: one grouped PR, merged automatically when CI is green
GitHub Actions majors (a new action or a new runner image) get a human review. The runners are pinned on purpose (see ci.yml): a new Ubuntu waits for a Playwright image built on it
Lit gets its own PR and a human review
Starters (apps/examples/*): the frameworks and tooling in one PR, merged automatically when the smoke test is green. The default ignorePaths skip **/examples/**; the list above keeps the rest of it
Starters: scripts/sync-versions.mjs owns the argus-table ranges (pnpm version-packages)
Starters: majors (a new React, Vue or Angular) get a human review
Peer dependency ranges are part of the published contract: widen them by hand, never narrow them
Playwright is pinned to the browsers in the cloud dev container and the CI image: bump the npm packages and the Docker image together, by hand
TypeScript 7 (the Go port) waits until typescript-eslint supports it
engines states the oldest versions we support, not the ones we run: raise it by hand
.nvmrc names a major (setup-node takes its latest release): only a new major is an update, and it gets a human review
@types/node follows the oldest Node in engines (22), so code doesn't use newer APIs
Majors (a new Node, pnpm, Ubuntu runner, framework…) wait on the Dependency Dashboard: a PR opens only when its box is ticked
